commit.message:
Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/master' into wh-2.10.6Upgrade

* origin/master:
  Locks should one enter if acquired
  sentinel: catch TimeoutError as well
  [sentinel] update master address if it changes.
  One more test for good measure.
  remove unneeded assertion.
  [tests] Write some tests to handle new logic in blocking connection pool.
  Remove unneded code.
  [bugfix] Implement the connection pool fixes onto the blocking connection pool.
  fixes the various scenarios where ConnectionPool.disconnect() and Connection.disconnect() were ripping connections out from under the threads or processes that owned them

travis/tox: Include python3.7 in builds

Summary: Adds python3.7 for test/builds in travis & tox.  In the case of
a conflict this commit can likely be ignored.

python redis-py: Pin pytest to <4.0.0 to avoid fixture breaking change

Summary: pytest made a backwards incompatible change in 4.0.0 that
throws errors with how fixtures are used in this library (causing the
entire test to fail).  This commit pins pytest to <4.0.0 to sidestep the
issue (the entire setup script seems to be streamlined upstream, so this
code should be safe to get rid of if there's any conflicts).

Locks should one enter if acquired

Backports a fix from upstream

https://github.com/andymccurdy/redis-py/commit/c99d2b98ff928a0709ee0453b60002e3e1254674

issues.title: Achieve parity in do_acquire with upstream redis-py repo
issues.body:
Achieve parity with the current version of redis-py, which fixes a possible bug that results in locks being acquired without expirations being set
Discovered through the investigation of https://app.asana.com/0/1202371958531131/1203556149319920/f
Relevant: (https://github.com/redis/redis-py/issues/554)

Risk: Breaks Redis servers with version < 2.6.12

Code change itself seems relatively low risk, but I'm not sure about how to best test the changes thoroughly before merging

Might be unnecessary if @jdunck plans to do work on catching our redis-py fork up to the upstream repo

issues.title: Upgrade Redis-py to 2.10.6
issues.body: Summary: Pulls the code up to 2.10.6 from `andymccurdy/redis-py`.  I also included one commit to pin pytest to <4.0.0 (otherwise my tests would fail with fixture errors, there was a backwards incompatible change in 4.0.0).
